title: Retry a VCF Installer depot replacement without duplicate effect
prompt:
Implement the unfinished `VcfInstallerClient.java` as a dependency-free Java 17 client for the VMware Cloud Foundation Installer 9.1 `updateDepotSettings` operation. Keep the implementation in that single Java file, use only the Java standard library, and preserve the supplied public API. Do not edit the harness, contract, or provenance files.

The focused contract in `docs/contract.json` was derived directly from `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`; `docs/official_sources.json` records the spec path, commit, and every operationId used. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Call only the named `updateDepotSettings` operation: `PUT /v1/system/settings/depot`.

`updateDepotSettings(DepotUpdate update, int maxRetries)` replaces the online VMware depot credentials. Require `downloadToken` to be a nonblank string no longer than the specification maximum of 32 characters. Treat a null or blank `downloadActivationCode` as unset. Validate `maxRetries` as an integer from 0 through 5; it counts attempts allowed after the first. Reject invalid credentials or retry counts locally with `IllegalArgumentException` before making a network request. Serialize the representation exactly once and retry only an HTTP 500 response or an ambiguous `IOException` transport failure. Never retry interruption, HTTP 400, or any other HTTP status. Accept exactly HTTP 202 with an `application/json` response object whose `vmwareAccount.downloadToken` and optional `downloadActivationCode` match the submitted effective values. Report exhausted transport failures, rejected HTTP responses, and invalid accepted responses with `IOException`; otherwise fail without putting either credential into an exception message.

Make the commit-before-error case safe: every retry must reuse the same URI, headers, and exact UTF-8 body bytes. This PUT replaces one stable resource, so do not change it to POST, add an attempt identifier, or vary the representation between attempts. The raw target must be exactly `/v1/system/settings/depot`, without a query string or bare `?`. Send exactly one each of `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`, `Accept: application/json`, and `Content-Type: application/json`; use a fixed content length rather than chunked transfer.

The compact request body is `{"vmwareAccount":{"downloadToken":<JSON string>}}` when the activation code is unset. If it is set, add only `downloadActivationCode` inside `vmwareAccount`. Omit all other optional contract properties rather than sending blank strings, nulls, false, zero, or empty objects: `username`, `password`, `status`, and `message` inside `vmwareAccount`, and top-level `offlineAccount` and `depotConfiguration`. Correctly JSON-escape runtime credential strings.

Run `bash protected_tests/verify.sh`. `TestMain` starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port. The mock serves only the operation named by the contract and writes a flushed JSONL request log for the test. It commits the first valid replacement and then returns the contract's HTTP 500 response; the exact retry receives HTTP 202. The verifier asserts the complete request wire shape, byte-identical attempts, optional-field omission, retry/error policy, successful response decoding, and one semantic mutation despite two HTTP requests. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint.
scenario: A depot replacement commits before the first HTTP 500 is returned, so an exact retry must complete without producing a second semantic effect.
